newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Final decision on media directive unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Final decision on media directive unlikely.

text.p: The European Commission is unlikely to adopt finally the draft media concentration directive when it meets on Wednesday, a Commission spokeswoman said on Monday.

Although support for the proposal in the executive seems to have increased since it was sent back to the drawing board last September, the Strasbourg meeting is unlikely to have sufficient time to fine tune the document, she said.
The plan the Commission will consider at its weekly meeting focuses on protecting the single market by harmonising divergent rules throughout the EU guaranteeing media pluralism.
"We think that another discussion would be helpful," said the spokeswoman.
Under the approach adopted by the Commission companies would not be able to extend their control of a country's television and radio stations once their audience share reaches a certain level.

According to a document made available to Reuters the ceiling has been set at 30 percent for owners operating in only one field, whether it be television or radio, and an average of 10 percent per medium for those operating in several areas, including the written press.

The plans -- drawn up in response to a demand from the European Parliament for a brake on over-concentration in the interests of democracy -- were put on the backburner last September after failing to muster sufficient support from the 20 Commissioners.
EU officials said some Commissioners remained opposed to having a binding directive.
